title: time-to-first-token-and-cache-warmth-observability-notebook
content:
Purpose:
This is a working notebook for defining a compact observability surface focused on Time-to-First-Token (TTFT) and cache-warmth signals that matter for tokenized inference economics and user perceived latency. Goal is to produce: metric defs, tracing anchors, cheap probe recipes, and a lightweight dashboard skeleton operators can use for fast rollouts and postmortems.

Context / why this is different:
- Many existing dashboards focus on end-to-end P50/P95 token latency and KV eviction counts. TTFT correlates more directly with UX for streaming/chat flows.
- Cache-warmth (prefix/KV hit distribution by tenant/model/version) explains TTFT variance and tail behavior during model rollouts or cold starts.
- Need a compact set of metrics and trace anchors so oncall can triage without digging through huge trace volumes.

Definitions (working):
- TTFT_request_ms: time from request received to first token start-of-stream emitted (ms).
- model-queue-delay_ms: time request spent queued behind batching or warmup tasks before execution.
- kv-prefetch-latency_ms: latency of KV prefetch ops when used (only measured when prefetch fired).
- kv-hit-rate_prefix: fraction of requests where prefix keys were present in KV cache at dispatch.
- prefix-warmth-index: rolling window (1h) of weighted kv-hit-rate_prefix across top 20 tenants.
- cold-eviction-rate: evictions per hour for model shard / tenant pair normalized by shard size.
- prefill-throughput_tps: number of prefix prefetch requests per second (used to track probe load).
- ttft-tail-ratio: P95 / P50 for TTFT_request_ms (easy health signal for tail regressions).

Notes on cardinality and labels (practical):
- Keep high-cardinality labels to a minimum on alerting metrics. Use tenant/model/version only for session-level panels and drilldowns.
- Primary aggregation keys: model_family, region, deployment_tier (hosted/dedicated/private), probe_type.

Tracing anchors (lightweight):
- Span layout: request.receive -> request.auth -> batching.enqueue -> batching.dispatch -> runtime.exec -> kv.prefetch -> runtime.first_token_emit -> streaming.pipe -> response.sent
- Anchor points to capture: batching.dispatch (batch size tag), kv.prefetch (hit/miss boolean tag), runtime.first_token_emit (latency), runtime.exec (compute_time_ms), response.sent (bytes_out)
- Minimal span sampling: always sample traces where TTFT_request_ms > 2x baseline OR where kv-hit-rate_prefix == 0 and model_family in top10. Otherwise probabilistic sample 0.5%.

Dashboard wireframe (panels & drilldowns):
- Overview row: global TTFT P50/P90/P95, ttft-tail-ratio, request rate, error count (generation_error).
- Cache warmth row: prefix-warmth-index (line per region), kv-hit-rate_prefix heatmap by model_family (small multiples), cold-eviction-rate histogram.
- Queueing & batching row: model-queue-delay_ms quantiles, avg batch_size, batching.delay_by_model.
- Traces & probes row: sample traces count, probe success/failure rate, prefill-throughput_tps.
- Cost guardrails: token-cost-per-second (approx), probe-cost-estimate, telemetry-query-cost (daily).
- Drilldown: tenant selector -> show top offending requests, recent traces, recent cold-evictions, per-tenant probe timeline.

Probe designs (cheap, safe):
- Passive probe: annotate a tiny fraction (0.1%) of real traffic with a prefetch header; measure kv-hit-rate_prefix + TTFT to estimate correlation. Low cost, safe for production.
- Active probe (scheduled): 10 probes/min per region scoped to top models only; request prefixes exactly match common UX start tokens. Tag with probe_type=active
- Probe cost control: gate active probes behind quota per deployment, allow emergency-disable via feature flag.

Alerting heuristics (draft):
- P95 TTFT spike: fire if P95 TTFT_request_ms increases by >50% vs 1h baseline AND ttft-tail-ratio > 2.5 for 5m.
- Warmth collapse: kv-hit-rate_prefix for top-3 models drops >30% vs 1h in a region -> page oncall.
- Eviction storm: cold-eviction-rate > X per shard (TBD) -> page and mute prefetchers.

Sampling & retention tradeoffs:
- Keep full-trace retention short (72h) for sampled traces; retain indexed anchors/metadata (span counts, tags) for 30d.
- Use adaptive sampling: increase sample rate for tenants showing TTFT anomalies.

Implementation notes / instrumentation TODOs:
- [ ] Add TTFT_request_ms metric at ingress gateway with request_id propagated.
- [ ] Emit kv-prefetch.* spans with hit/miss and latency tags from runtime prefetch layer.
- [ ] Ship prefix-warmth-index computed in metrics pipeline (store per-model hourly rollups).
- [ ] Dashboard prototype in grafana under /observability/team-ops/ttft-cache-warmth.
- [ ] Safety flag to throttle active probes per-tenant.

Open questions and tradeoffs (notes to self):
- How tied should TTFT be to streaming vs non-streaming paths? Some models may emit first token faster if streaming start is favored. Need a consistent definition at ingress.
- Prefix-warmth semantics across multi-model fanout: when fanout to auxiliary rerank models, who owns the warmth metric? Propose primary-model ownership with auxiliary as secondary dimension.
- Cost vs fidelity: can we compute prefix-warmth offline from traces rather than emit high-cardinality live metrics? Might be acceptable for long-window analysis but not for alerts.

Short-term milestones (next 8 weeks):
- Week 1-2: instrument TTFT and kv-prefetch spans (runtime + gateway). Owner: Rohan.
- Week 3: basic dashboard P0 panels + 0.1% passive probe rollout. Owner: Avery.
- Week 4-6: add active probe flow behind feature flag, implement probe cost quota. Owner: Morgan.
- Week 7-8: alert tuning + runbook draft and tabletop. Owner: eng-observability rotation.

Runbook sketches (very brief):
- If P95 TTFT spikes: check batching.queue_delay -> check kv-hit-rate_prefix -> check recent helm deploys and model rollouts -> escalate to runtime oncall if compute_time_ms increased.
- If warmth collapse: disable active probes, investigate eviction logs, check autoscaler activity and recent shard resizes.

Notes / references:
- Related: CONFLUENCE-OBS-5243 (kv cache priming strategy), JIRA-OBS-2187 (ttft spike investigation template).
- Implementation prototypes: github.com/redwood/obs-probes/pull/62 (passive probe POC).

Quick wins / experiments to try ASAP:
- Compute correlation matrix (TTFT vs kv-hit-rate_prefix vs batch_size) for top 5 models over last 7 days. If correlation > 0.6, prioritize prefetching.
- Run active probe at 10x reduced load in staging across models with long prefixes to validate noisiness.

Notes to reviewers: this is intentionally compact — the aim is a small, operator-friendly surface. Feedback: ways to simplify labels, safe sampling defaults, and probe quotas welcome.

Signed-off: Avery (owner) — ping in #obs-ops for quick sync
